chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, both together from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Thal'abah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Every oath upon which a man swears that he will not do it, from what has benefit for him in this world and the Hereafter, there is no expiation upon him. And rather, the expiation is when a man swears, 'By Allah I will not commit adultery,' 'By Allah I will not drink wine,' 'By Allah I will not steal,' 'By Allah I will not be treacherous,' and the like of this, 'I will not disobey,' then he does it, so upon him is the expiation with regards to it.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between an oath that requires expiation and one that does not in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between oaths of abstention from beneficial acts, which incur no expiation, and those of abstention from virtuous duties or general obedience, which do. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the intent and nature of the prohibited act, distinguishing between mere convenience and moral or religious obligation. The hadith serves as a foundational text for understanding the conditions under which an oath becomes binding and requires kaffarah upon violation.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, both together from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Sa’alba, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Every oath one swears upon that he would not do it, from what for him therein is a benefit regarding the world and the Hereafter, so there is no expiation upon him. But rather, the expiation is in if the man swear, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup> I will not commit adultery!’ and ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup> I will not drink the wine!’ and ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup> I will not steal!’ and ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup> I will not be treacherous’, and the likes of this, and ‘I will not disobey!, then he does it, so upon him is the expiation with regards to it’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa all from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Tha’labah from Zurarah who has narrated the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Every act for which one takes an oath not to do it and the act is beneficial in this and in the hereafter, there is no expiation for it. Kaffarah (expiation) becomes obligatory when one takes an oath and says, ‘By Allah I will not commit fornication, by Allah I will not drink wine, by Allah I will not steal, by Allah I will not act treacherously and so on and I will not disobey, but he does, then Kaffarah (expiation) becomes obligatory.’”
